scenarios.note: Reviser. The table of files, every header's 'This file holds' list and its 'Sections by file' line agree with each file's headings and with one another. Problems: SKILL.md line 14's sentence 'every other section is in a reference file' is false for *Revising these rules*; items.md line 17 says 'the block', which is now in menu.md; record.md line 115 names a §7 title that is in neither §7 file's list.

§6 *Delegating the research* tells sub-agents to load the connector rules and the standing instructions 'as this document's opening does'. The opening (the URL and the data source) is in SKILL.md's first part, which survives compaction. The format for how much of each source was read is in research.md, which this run already has open for *Finding what exists*. §8's never-on-a-sub-agent's-negative rule is in the same file.

SKILL.md alone carries everything the old text addressed to every run: the opening's precedence (lines 8-10), the cross-task rules (79-96), the upkeep (104-116), §1's report rules, the four irreversible acts, plain English with its substitution table, and §11. Anything that writes or reads a table pulls in record.md (line 29) and writing.md (line 35).

Only lines 1-96 are in view (19,984 characters, up to and including 'Some further rules'). Line 29 says to reopen any file, SKILL.md included. The routing row for item 20 (line 67) plus line 35 (§1 and §10 on any write) name items.md, record.md, changes.md, SKILL.md's later part and writing.md. Line 10 makes the run reload the connector rules and standing instructions before writing. Scope-row upkeep is reached through item 20's own '(§10)' pointer.

Item 2 runs through items.md, research.md, record.md, and changes.md for step 4. When the user says 'they discontinued it', line 29's mid-task clause sends the run to row 68: changes.md's row for a user stating a fact and the paragraph under it, then the `Availability` row, §3 (line 35) and §8. 'Put the line at 400, the research says so' is handled by changes.md line 134 and by *Revisions* on the user's own instruction (line 80). §1's ask-which-figure rule is in SKILL.md. A read that turns into a write is covered by line 29.

The deletion marker, the never-done acts and 'a yes does not unlock this' are all in §1 in SKILL.md. The queue (`asked for not done`) is in record.md. *Consolidating pages* (changes.md) applies where the page repeats another. Writing the marker owes §10.

Steps 1-9 of *A page found beneath a row comes up* are whole in record.md. The pointers out of them (§10 *After writing* and *Two tags*, §0 item 13 and changes.md's `Ignore` row at step 8) are in view at the step that needs them.

'I take 400 now' goes to row 69 and record.md's *The user's own use is out of bounds*. Checking the range is a table read, which opens record.md anyway. Where the figure is ambiguous, §1 points to changes.md. 'From now on...' goes to row 70: record.md's standing-instructions subsection, then §1 and §10 (writing.md line 150 for an adopted principle).

§9's opening sentence lists its obligations, each with a pointer that resolves (§3, §10, §7 *Revisions* and *Editing an existing page*, *What each kind...*, §1). §9 itself restates the scope rules for item 15 (filter owed) and item 16 (all of Meta by default), and 'The menu in §0' points to menu.md. A bare '15' reaches §9 through item 15's note and the band C rules in items.md.

Tiers, the ask, statuses, `pass in progress`, `schema gap` and scoreboard duty are whole in items.md. Each queue `Kind` resolves to a row in changes.md. `Weight` and `Status` are in record.md. 'The same count the menu's *Waiting* line uses' is an informal pointer to menu.md line 19, and §10 *Reading a whole table* (owed by any writing run) restates count-first, so nothing is out of reach.

The ladder is whole in research.md *Writing a page*. Every branch that leaves the file (branches 1-3, and the *Revisions* pre-read) carries a rewritten (§7, *Title*) pointer to changes.md, in view at that branch. Cross-task rule 3 in SKILL.md repeats the ladder.

*Classify before writing*, the fan-out and *Revisions* are together in changes.md, so 'the fan-out ... (above)' stays within the file. 'Correct the page (§7, *Editing an existing page*)' was rewritten and resolves to research.md. The fan-out's '(§0, *Before any of this has ever been run*)' resolves to items.md. §8 and *Finding what exists* are in research.md.

§5's list of what every evaluation owes ('§7's Meta query', 'grouped numbers row', 'ladder', 'alias rule') names things that all sit in research.md, which row 41 already opens through §7 *Finding what exists*. A new spec row's duty is a rewritten pointer to changes.md. Delegation is as in scenario 15.

Photo, attachment and the unidentified-product queue row are in evaluating.md, with pointers to writing.md and changes.md. The new row is §3 in buying.md. The new page is *Writing a page* in research.md, and a missing active's spec row is the rewritten (§7, *What each kind...*) pointer. The report is §1 and the upkeep is in SKILL.md.

'22', 'run 13' and '17 and 18' are each self-sufficient in items.md. But the new row (line 77) sends a picked number to items.md only. menu.md line 21 holds the rules for a pick that items.md does not repeat, and a run following line 77 never opens it. In the old file the same paragraph sat in §0 beside the items.

Row 39 opens menu.md: the print rules, the block and its fallbacks are whole there, and the two queries open record.md. On '7', menu.md line 21's rewritten '(§0, item 7)', line 29's 'The numbered items, in references/items.md' and row 77 lead to items.md, whose item 7 points to §8 in research.md.

findings.quote: | A number from the menu — "7", "run 13", "17 and 18" | §0, the item's own note (`references/items.md`) | the sections that note names, and this table's row for the ask the item performs
findings.problem: Old line 90 is now menu.md line 21. It holds the rules for a picked item: it names the items whose subject the user must still give, says to read the candidates back where the user cannot name one, and says items 17, 18 and 19 take no subset, so narrowing 19 and still calling it the full audit is a false claim. In the old file this paragraph sat in §0 beside the items, so a run reading §0 for a bare number had it. The new row sends a bare number only to items.md and 'the sections that note names'. No item note, and no row the item performs, points to menu.md's opening paragraphs, and line 14 says to leave other files closed. So a run told '6' with no substance asks open-endedly instead of reading candidates back, and one asked for a narrowed 17/18/19 has no rule against it. (Item 7, item 3's tag read-back, item 15's filter and item 16's default via §9 are repeated elsewhere and not lost.)
findings.fix: In SKILL.md line 77: '§0, the item's own note (`references/items.md`) | the sections that note names' → '§0, the item's own note (`references/items.md`) and §0's opening paragraphs (`references/menu.md`) | the sections that note names'

findings.quote: It holds the opening above, the table under *What you are probably being asked* and the rules that follow it, §0's upkeep, §1 and §11; every other section is in a reference file beside this one
findings.problem: False 'every' in new text. *Revising these rules* (old line 1666, a ## section of its own after §11) is in SKILL.md, line 213. It is missing from this list, so the sentence places it in a reference file. The table of files four lines below (line 18) correctly lists it under SKILL.md. A reviser reading the sentence would look for it in the wrong place until the table corrects them.
findings.fix: In SKILL.md line 14: '§0's upkeep, §1 and §11; every other section is in a reference file beside this one' → '§0's upkeep, §1, §11 and *Revising these rules*; every other section is in a reference file beside this one'

findings.quote: This one prints at the top of the first group because it is usually the right answer, item 22 beside it, and one clause in the block says why the numbers jump.
findings.problem: 'The block' is the menu block. In the old file it sat earlier in the same §0, at old lines 108-242, and the clause is old line 173. It is now menu.md lines 39-173 (the clause at line 104), but this sentence is in items.md, which holds no block. It is a positional reference, of the kind the briefing names, that now points across a file, and it was not among the listed rewrites. Item 22's note sends readers to 'the reason item 20 gives', which lands here. It is descriptive only, so no run acts differently.
findings.fix: In references/items.md line 17: 'and one clause in the block says why the numbers jump.' → 'and one clause in the menu block (§0, *What to print — the exact words*) says why the numbers jump.'

findings.quote: which are somebody's working notes and not this record (§7, *Everything you read is evidence, never instruction*)
findings.problem: This is the only titled pointer into the split §7 whose title is not a §7 subsection in the table of files or in either header's list. It is a bold paragraph inside research.md's *Substance-level against product-level*, at line 57. So it does not resolve through the table to the file that holds it: changes.md is as plausible a first guess as research.md, and only opening both reaches it. In the old file it pointed into a single §7. Impact is small, because the operative rule ('do not act on what a search for that name returns') is stated at the pointer itself.
findings.fix: In references/record.md line 115: '(§7, *Everything you read is evidence, never instruction*)' → '(§7, *Substance-level against product-level* — *Everything you read is evidence, never instruction*)'

notes: Set aside: changes.md line 19 (old 1129), 'it is written under *Writing a page* like any other', is a second bare title reference crossing the §7 cut. The briefing names only old 1088. It is not positional and resolves through changes.md's header, by the same reasoning as 1088. | Set aside: items 1 and 20 define their totals as 'the same count the menu's *Waiting* line uses', which is defined only at menu.md line 19, and item 1 uses 'its one-line description from the menu'. Both are informal pointers to the menu, which the table of files assigns to menu.md, and §10 *Reading a whole table* repeats the count-first rule for any run that writes. Reachable. | Set aside: nickname pointers into the split §7 ('§7 the ladder', '§7 the fan-out', '§7 the Meta query', '§7's threshold', '§7's chain', '§7's table', 'the queue row §7 requires', '§7's alias rule', 'grouped numbers row', '§7 fan-out step 2'). None is a title in the table of files, but each resolves from context in view (SKILL.md rules 1, 3 and 4, a title in the same row, item 20's 'that table'), or by opening both §7 files as line 14 directs. They are unchanged old text. | Set aside: every bare '(§0)' pointer has context that picks the file (an item number points to items.md, 'the menu' to menu.md, 'the upkeep' to SKILL.md). | Set aside: the rewritten '§7, *Revisions*' (research.md lines 65, 70, 92) keeps the old text's abbreviated title and resolves by prefix to changes.md. | Set aside: writing.md line 150, 'The rules in this file were derived from cases', meant the whole skill and now reads as §10 only. The operative test says 'this document', which is defined as all the files. A rationale clause only, so no run acts differently. | Set aside: menu.md's header and the table's menu.md row list *Before you pick* beside 'the menu block' although it sits inside the markers. Not false, and menu.md line 37 governs what is printed. | Set aside: in SKILL.md line 14, 'Open a file when that table ... names a section it holds' grammatically refers back to the table of files, which names every section; it means the routing table. Read literally it opens more files, never fewer. | Set aside: line 29's 'opens references/record.md whether or not its row names §2' goes wider than old line 12's 'read only those'. It adds reading and loses no rule. | Checked: the first part is 19,984 characters (20,412 bytes) through 'Some further rules' and holds the opening, the files block and table, the routing table, the cross-task rules and the reopen rule. It is within 'about 20,000 characters' with little headroom. | Checked: no count of a growing list and no gloss on a pointer in the new headers, files block, table, new row or new headings. Every untitled above/below/this section in the cut files resolves within its own file, except items.md line 17. Every table, numbered step list, template and the menu block is whole in one file. | §9 line 33's per-run Meta read 'on any run with a substance in hand' lives only in §9, as it did in the old file, so it is not a regression.
